cards.explanation: The answer is that the sun will be darkened. Jesus says that after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened. He says it plainly, so there's nothing to decode. Sit with that for a second, friends, because Jesus doesn't rush it.
The answer is False. Jesus says the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light. Neither one is working. The text says both go dark, so no backup light is coming from the moon.

The answer is True. Jesus says the stars will fall from the sky. It comes right after the verse about the sun and the moon. I read that line twice, friends, because Jesus says it and I take it seriously.

The answer is that the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Jesus says it just that way. Whatever those powers are, they don't stay steady. It's like a counter when somebody slams the oven door, except this is the heavens.

The answer is False. In all that dark, Jesus says they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds. He doesn't mention Elijah anywhere in this passage. The Son of Man is Jesus' name for Himself (Mark 2:10).

The answer is with great power and glory. Jesus says they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory. The sky goes dark, and then comes that. Not a quiet entrance, friends.

The answer is GATHER, friends! Jesus says He will send out the angels to gather His elect. The verse names the errand, and the errand is gathering. I'd sing about it if my mustache could carry a tune.

The answer is from the four winds. Jesus says the angels gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven. That's a wide reach, bakers. The gathering goes from one far edge to the other.

The answer is that the branches get tender and sprout leaves. Jesus says that when the fig branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know summer is near. The branches tell you before the season shows up. It's a sign anybody can read just by looking.
The answer is summer. Jesus says that as soon as the branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near. The tree gives the early notice, friends. Anybody watching it can tell.

The answer is that He is near, right at the door. Jesus says that when you see these things happening, know that He is near, right at the door. He turns the fig tree into a lesson about the very things He's been describing. The tree shows summer coming, and the signs show Him near.

The answer is True. Jesus tells them to learn a lesson from the fig tree: leaves mean summer is near. Then He says that when they see these things happening, they should know that He is near, right at the door. Watching the branches and watching the signs work the same way, friends.

The answer is that His words will never pass away. Jesus says heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will never pass away. That puts His words on firmer ground than the sky and the ground itself. Nothing in the whole passage is steadier, friends.

The answer is only the Father. Jesus says no one knows about that day or hour, but only the Father. So there's no guessing from me, and no guessing from anybody else. The knowing belongs to the Father.

The answer is True. Jesus says no one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father. The angels are right there in heaven, and even they don't know. That's why I don't guess the day, friends, I just keep my ovens ready.

The answer is to be on guard and stay alert. Jesus says, "Be on your guard and stay alert! For you do not know when the appointed time will come." Not knowing the time is exactly why He says to stay ready. That's why my ovens stay warm, bakers.

The answer is his own task. In Jesus' picture, the man puts each servant in charge of his own task. Each servant has something of his own to do, friends. The doorkeeper gets his instructions too, to keep watch.
The answer is watch. The man instructs the doorkeeper to keep watch. That job sits at the door, so the doorkeeper's eyes stay open for the master coming home.

The answer is from evening to morning. Jesus lists evening, midnight, when the rooster crows, and the morning. Put those together and they cover the stretch from evening to morning. The master could come back at any one of them, friends.

The answer is that he might find you sleeping. Jesus says, "Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping." The danger isn't only that the master comes back, it's that he finds you asleep. That's why Jesus says to keep watch, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!” It starts with the four who asked Him privately (Mark 13:3), but it doesn't stop there. The call to keep watch is for everyone, friends, and that includes you.
